compensating.why: hop 1 leaves series of two items as they are
hop 2 takes the period of the first item as the reference
hop 4 asks the next step not to notify

ownership_reason: Only the gold decides, for each leading item, whether its time period lies more than the maximum age before the reference period, removes those items and notifies the listeners of the series. Hop 1 only checks that the series has more than one item, hop 2 only reads the serial index of the last period, hops 3 and 4 pass the values on. Once the gold has sent the event for a series it left unchanged, no caller can withdraw it. The gold notifies through Series.fireSeriesChanged(), documented as signalling to the listeners that the series has been changed (a SeriesChangeEvent is an event with details of a change to a series); the variant sends that signal when no item was removed. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the intact sibling overload TimeSeries.removeAgedItems(long, boolean) does the same step (`if (removed && notify) fireSeriesChanged()`), TimeSeries.delete(RegularTimePeriod) fires only when the period is present and TimeSeries.clear() only when the series is not empty, and the facade's own @param notify says the event is sent IF any items are removed; testRemoveAgedItems2 (the sibling: no event when nothing is removed) and testDelete2 (no event for an absent period) pass, as do testAddOrUpdate and testSetMaximumItemCount, whose edits reach the chain with notify = false.
